prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the claims-triage agent (home and motor claims assessment within delegated authority) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: shopping around at renewal. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 1)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When a renewal comes in much cheaper than the previous year, I should check whether the cover has been quietly reduced, because a lower premium can hide a higher excess or missing optional benefits."},{"type":"fact","content":"When a member says they are shopping around, I should ask what level of cover they are comparing, because like-for-like comparison only works if the insured limits, excesses and add-ons match."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the renewal date is close, I should remind myself that hurried comparisons often miss details, so I should encourage the member to check the policy summary rather than just the headline price."},{"type":"preference","content":"When a member has found a cheaper quote elsewhere, I prefer to ask whether the new insurer covers accidental damage, personal belongings and courtesy support, as these differences can affect claim outcomes later."},{"type":"fact","content":"When shopping around has led a member to change insurer, I should note that gaps in cover can happen if the new policy starts after the old one ends, especially where mid-term changes or cancelled renewals are involved."},{"type":"observation","content":"When a member is comparing motor renewals, I should look out for differences in named driver terms, mileage limits and commuting use, because these can matter more than a small premium saving."},{"type":"observation","content":"When a home renewal quote drops sharply, I should consider whether the rebuild sum insured has been adjusted down, because underinsurance can become a problem if the member later makes a large claim."},{"type":"fact","content":"When a member shops around every year, I should not assume disloyalty or dissatisfaction; it is often a normal way for households to manage budgets, so the conversation should stay factual and neutral."},{"type":"preference","content":"When I see a renewal with a higher excess than before, I prefer to point that out clearly, because members often focus on the premium and only notice the excess when they first need to claim."},{"type":"observation","content":"When a member mentions switching at renewal after a claim, I should remember that continuity of disclosure matters, because questions from a new insurer about recent losses can affect acceptance and pricing."}]}
